newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo mayor said tied to Brazil bond scandal.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo mayor said tied to Brazil bond scandal.

text.p: A leading Brazilian senator on Tuesday accused Sao Paulo mayor Celso Pitta's wife of accepting favours from a bank suspected of profiting from a multi-million dollar bond scam, linking the mayor to the growing political scandal.
Sen. Roberto Requiao, who is heading a congressional probe into the bond scandal, told reporters he had evidence that Banco Vector had paid a car rental bill of $2,500 for Pitta's wife.

"Let's put an end to all this cynicism. It is obvious that people in the Sao Paulo mayor's office are involved in this right up to the roots of the hairs on their heads," Requiao told reporters on Tuesday.
Pitta issued a statement saying he was unaware Banco Vector had paid for his wife's car rental.
The congressional probe is looking into allegations that brokers and officials may have siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars through suspect municipal and state bond issues.
Several states and some cities are alleged to have sold bonds at well below market-prices, ensuring instant profits for brokers and others involved in the scheme.
The alleged car rental evidence comes shortly after the congressional committee discovered that a team of high level Sao Paulo City Hall officials helped mastermind the bond scam.

Pitta, Sao Paulo's first black mayor and a rising star in national politics, has denied any role in the scandal despite the fact that officials accused of designing the fraud worked directly under him when he was the city's finance secretary.
The mayor claims the investigation is an attempt by disgruntled rivals to push him out of office. However he has agreed to fire the four City Hall officials accused of being involved in the fraud.
Senators suspect the mayor was at least negligent if not directly involved in the bond fraud, in which at least $600 million in public monies disappeared.
They said the latest developments would increase pressure to have Pitta testify before the congressional committee as soon as possible.

The congressional probe into the bond scandal shook Brazil's financial community last month after the Central Bank closed down two banks and 14 small brokerages accused of profiting from the illegal scheme.
